newsitem.title: CANADA: Cominco Polaris workers become unionized.
newsitem.headline: Cominco Polaris workers become unionized.

text.p: The Canada Labour Relations Board has decided to allow 200 workers at Cominco Ltd's Polaris zinc mine to unionize, the United Steelworkers of America said on Friday.
The union said it will represent permanent employees but not temporary workers at the mine, located about 1,000 km north of Yellowknife near the North Pole.
The mine produces 250,000 tonnes of zinc and lead concentrate per year, a Cominco spokesman said. He said a total of 270 employees work at the site.
The labor relations board ruled in favor of the union this week after the union applied for certification last May, the Steelworkers said in a statement.

"We are pleased to welcome this unique group of miners into our union," said Ken Neumann, the Steelworkers' Western Canada director. "We look forward to negotiating a collective agreement with Cominco that recognizes their needs as workers in Canada's most northerly mining oppost."
Cominco said it will have to examine the labor board decision before deciding on its next step.
"It's too early to say how things will go from here," said spokesman Doug Horswill in Vancouver.
